own_solution.law: Static equilibrium of a rigid ladder: N = (m1+m2) g; torque about the foot gives wall force F_w = (0.5 m1 + 0.6 m2) g cot(theta); friction f = F_w; ground force = sqrt(N^2 + f^2)
assumptions: ladder in static equilibrium (does not slip)
uniform ladder, centre of mass at mid-length
person treated as a point load at 0.6 L

notes: N = 82*9.8 = 803.6 N; torque sum (0.5*117.6 + 0.6*686) = 470.4 N (per unit L). At 62 deg: cot = 0.531709, f = 250.12 N, |F| = sqrt(803.6^2 + 250.12^2) = 841.62 N. At 44 deg (tilted 18 deg closer to the ground): cot = 1.035530, f = 487.11 N, |F| = 939.71 N; this needs a friction coefficient of at least 0.606, and the problem states the ladder does not slip, so it is consistent. Length cancels from the torque balance (C). Earlier-experiment and shutter sentences are D. The scene clause about set-up vs final angle makes TCE71 (tilt before the person stands) and TD573 (tilt afterwards) both change the final angle. Numbered angle sentences all use 18 deg; T1EB2 and TA81B carry no number. 'Then tilted' in TD573 with the person standing on it is an unusual operation, hence slightly artificial.
